Launch the pilotr no-code app

Source: R/run_app.R
run_app.Rd

Runs the bundled Shiny app locally. When the package is installed, the app calls the package's functions directly. Running locally gives each user a private R process, so no one else's work waits on theirs.

Usage

run_app(..., async = NULL)

Arguments

...

passed to shiny::runApp() (e.g. port, launch.browser).

async

If TRUE (the default when 'future' and 'promises' are installed), the app runs each power analysis and power curve in a background R process. That leaves the app's own R process free for other sessions, such as a second browser tab, while the session that started the run waits for it. A parallel future plan you have set is used as it stands. Over a sequential plan, the default, run_app() sets a multisession plan of two workers while the app runs. Either way, the plan in force before the call is in force again once the app stops. With FALSE, power runs in the app's own R process and no plan is set.

Value

No return value; called for its side effect of launching the Shiny application, which blocks the R session until the app is closed.

Details

Each power analysis and power curve in the app runs in one R process, and the session that asked for it waits for the result. Its controls and outputs do not update until the run ends. For a heavy run, download the specification and call power_design() or power_mixed() from the console, where workers spreads the replicates over your local cores.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
run_app()
} # }
